plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following persons is explicitly empowered by Section 2(60) of the Companies Act, 2013 to be designated as an 'Officer who is in default'?
options: Every independent director in respect of all board decisions
A whole-time director
Any external statutory auditor
An independent legal advisor retained by the company
plain.explanation: Section 2(60) defines an 'officer who is in default' to include whole-time directors, key managerial personnel, and directors who have given their consent to proceedings or failed to take adequate steps. Independent directors are specifically excluded unless the contravention occurs without their knowledge or consent, or despite their due diligence. Therefore, whole-time directors are included.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the statutory minimum paid-up share capital requirement for a Private Company?
options: One Lakh Rupees
Five Lakh Rupees
Ten Lakh Rupees
There is no minimum paid-up share capital requirement prescribed
plain.explanation: By virtue of the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015, the requirement for a minimum paid-up share capital of Rs. 1 lakh for private companies and Rs. 5 lakhs for public companies was removed. Consequently, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Act now.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following entities is specifically *excluded* from the definition of 'Financial Institution' under Section 2(39) of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: A scheduled bank
The Industrial Finance Corporation of India
The Life Insurance Corporation of India
A non-banking financial company registered under the RBI Act
plain.explanation: Section 2(39) defines a financial institution to include a industrial finance corporation, a scheduled bank, the Life Insurance Corporation, etc. An NBFC is governed separately under the RBI Act and is not listed as a financial institution under this specific sub-section.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In relation to a holding company, a 'subsidiary company' as per Section 2(87) includes a company in which the holding company controls:
options: More than 25% of the total voting power
Not less than 35% of the total voting power
More than one-half of the total voting power
Exactly 50% of the total voting power
plain.explanation: Section 2(87) defines a subsidiary company as one in which the holding company controls the composition of the Board of Directors or exercises or controls more than one-half of the total voting power either on its own or together with one or more of its subsidiary companies.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: According to Section 2(20), the term 'Company' means a company formed and registered under this Act or under any:
options: Previous Company Law
Foreign Company Law
Partnership Act, 1932
Cooperative Societies Act, 1912
plain.explanation: Section 2(20) states that 'company' means a company formed and registered under this Act or under any previous company law, encompassing legislations like the Companies Act, 1956 and earlier acts.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following is an essential characteristic of a 'Government Company' as defined under Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Not less than 25% paid-up capital held by the Central Government
Not less than 50% paid-up capital held jointly by Central and State Governments
Not less than 51% paid-up capital held by a foreign government
Solely owned by statutory corporations created by Parliament
plain.explanation: Section 2(45) defines a Government Company as any company in which not less than 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, or by any State Government or Governments, or partly by the Central Government and partly by one or more State Governments.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with the incorporation of a company?
options: Section 3
Section 7
Section 9
Section 10
plain.explanation: Section 7 of the Companies Act, 2013 outlines the detailed procedure for the incorporation of a company, including filing documents with the Registrar and the issuance of the certificate of incorporation.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: A 'One Person Company' (OPC) can be formed by a natural person who is an Indian citizen and:
options: A resident in India only
Resident in India or otherwise
A non-resident Indian holding a PIO card
A resident in India for not less than 182 days in the previous calendar year
plain.explanation: As amended by the Companies (Incorporation) Second Amendment Rules, 2021, the residency requirement of being a resident in India for not less than 182 days has been reduced to 120 days, and an OPC can be incorporated by a natural person who is an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a minor be admitted as a member or nominee of a One Person Company (OPC) under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Yes, through a natural guardian
Yes, with prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal
No, a minor cannot become a member or nominee of an OPC
Yes, provided the minor's shares are fully paid-up
plain.explanation: As per the rules governing OPCs, a minor cannot become a member or nominee of the OPC or hold share with beneficial interest. Allowing a minor would contravene the contractual capacity requirements for company membership.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the legal effect of registration of a company under Section 9 of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: It creates a partnership among shareholders
It incorporates the company into a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional)
It transfers ownership of all promoter assets to the directors automatically
It grants the company tax exemption for the first five financial years
plain.explanation: Section 9 provides that from the date of incorporation mentioned in the certificate of incorporation, the subscribers shall be a body corporate capable of exercising all functions of an incorporated company with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional now).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 2(57), 'to hold' shares in a company includes being a beneficial owner of shares whose name is entered in the records of a:
options: Stock exchange
Depository
Registrar of Companies
National Company Law Tribunal
plain.explanation: Section 2(57) defines 'to hold' in relation to shares to include a person whose name is entered as a beneficial owner in the records of a depository, acknowledging dematerialized shareholding.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following definitions under Section 2 encompasses a company incorporated outside India that has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent?
options: Section 2(20) - Company
Section 2(42) - Foreign Company
Section 2(46) - Holding Company
Section 2(68) - Private Company
plain.explanation: Section 2(42) defines a 'foreign company' as any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: A company limited by guarantee may have a share capital. What is the liability of members in such a company in the event of winding up?
options: Unlimited liability up to personal assets
Up to the amount guaranteed and unpaid on shares held, if any
Strictly limited to the nominal value of the shares without any guarantee amount
Zero liability if the company is solvent
plain.explanation: Under Section 2(22), a company limited by guarantee means a company having the liability of its members limited by the memorandum to such amount as the members may respectively undertake to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up, plus any unpaid amount on shares if it has a share capital.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: An 'associate company' in relation to another company, as defined in Section 2(6), means a company in which that other company has:
options: Control of at least 10% of total voting power
Significant influence, which means control of at least 20% of total voting power or business control under an agreement
Control of exactly 50% of total voting power
Subsidiary control of more than 50% voting power
plain.explanation: Section 2(6) defines an associate company as a company in which that other company has a significant influence, which is defined as control of at least 20% of total voting power, or control of business under an agreement.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: According to Section 2(71), a 'Public Company' is a company which is not a private company and has a minimum paid-up share capital as:
options: May be prescribed
Not less than Rs. 5 Lakhs
Not less than Rs. 10 Lakhs
Not less than Rs. 1 Crore
plain.explanation: Section 2(71) defines a public company as a company which is not a private company and has a minimum paid-up share capital, as may be prescribed. Presently, no minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed by rules.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company be treated as a private company for all exemptions under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Yes, because its articles contain all restrictions under Section 2(68)
No, a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company is deemed to be a public company for the purposes of the Act
Yes, provided its turnover is below 100 crores
No, unless approved by the Central Government
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 2(71), a private company which is a subsidiary of a public company shall be deemed to be a public company for the purposes of this Act even where such subsidiary company continues to be a private company in its articles.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 contains definitions of various terms used throughout the statute?
options: Section 1
Section 2
Section 3
Section 4
plain.explanation: Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 is the interpretation clause containing definitions of various technical and legal terms used across the Act.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 2(84), 'share' means a share in the share capital of a company and includes:
options: Debentures
Stock
Public deposits
Bonds
plain.explanation: Section 2(84) defines 'share' to mean a share in the share capital of a company and includes stock, except where a distinction between stock and share is expressed or implied.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following is excluded from the definition of 'deposit' under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014?
options: Amount raised by issuance of non-convertible debentures not constituting a charge on assets
Any amount received from a relative of a director of the company, accompanied by a declaration that it is not out of borrowed funds
Unsecured loans taken from commercial banks
Advance received against sale of goods to be delivered within 365 days
plain.explanation: Under the Deposit Rules, amounts received from a relative of a director (or member in case of private company) accompanied by a written declaration that the money is not given out of borrowed funds are excluded from the definition of 'deposits'. Advances for goods within 365 days are also excluded, but bank loans are borrowings, not relative advances.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the extent of territorial jurisdiction of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Whole of India
Whole of India including Jammu & Kashmir and all Union Territories
India and foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies
Only mainland states of India excluding Special Economic Zones
plain.explanation: Section 1(2) specifies that the Companies Act, 2013 extends to the whole of India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which provision governs the incorporation of a One Person Company (OPC), restricting membership to a natural person?
options: Section 3
Section 7
Section 8
Section 9
plain.explanation: Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013 specifies formation of companies, providing that a company may be formed for any lawful purpose by seven or more persons (public), two or more persons (private), or one person (OPC).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In the context of 'dormant company' under Section 455, a company is classified as dormant if it has not been carrying on any business or operation, or has not made any significant accounting transaction during the last:
options: One financial year
Two consecutive financial years
Three consecutive financial years
Five financial years
plain.explanation: Section 455 provides that a company which has not been carrying on any business or operation, or has not made any significant accounting transaction during the last two consecutive financial years, or has not filed financial statements and annual returns during the last two consecutive financial years, may apply to the Registrar to obtain dormant status.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following activities does *not* constitute a 'significant accounting transaction' for a dormant company under Section 455?
options: Payment of fees by a company to the Registrar
Payments of statutory dues to authorities
Allotment of shares for cash
Office space rent paid to maintain its registered office
plain.explanation: Section 455 defines 'significant accounting transaction' as any transaction other than: (i) payment of fees by a company to the Registrar; (ii) payments of statutory dues; (iii) allotment of shares to fulfill requirements of the Act; and (iv) office maintenance expenses. Allotment of shares for cash is an active financial operation.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following bodies corporate is specifically excluded from the definition of a 'Body Corporate' under Section 2(11)?
options: A cooperative society registered under any law relating to cooperative societies
A limited liability partnership
A foreign company
A public financial institution
plain.explanation: Section 2(11) defines 'body corporate' to include a company incorporated outside India, but specifically excludes (i) a co-operative society registered under any law relating to co-operative societies, and (ii) any other body corporate specified by the Central Government.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What does Section 2(68) mandate regarding the maximum number of members in a private company?
options: Maximum 50 members
Maximum 100 members
Maximum 200 members
No limit on maximum members
plain.explanation: Section 2(68) defines a private company as one having a minimum paid-up share capital as prescribed, and which by its articles restricts the right to transfer its shares and limits the number of its members to 200 (excluding employee-members and past employee-members).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In computing the limit of 200 members in a private company, which of the following persons are excluded?
options: Persons who are in the employment of the company
Persons who were formerly in the employment of the company and were members while in that employment and have continued to be members after the employment ceased
Both (A) and (B)
All preference shareholders holding shares for more than 2 years
plain.explanation: The proviso to Section 2(68) states that where two or more persons hold one or more shares in a company jointly, they shall be treated as a single member, and persons in employment and persons who were formerly in employment and continue as members after cessation of employment are excluded from the limit of 200.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with companies with charitable and other objects (License under Section 8)?
options: Section 7
Section 8
Section 9
Section 12
plain.explanation: Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with formation of companies with charitable objects, promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment, etc., intending to apply profits towards promoting its objects and prohibiting dividend payment.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a partnership firm be a member of a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: No, partnership firms cannot be members
Yes, a partnership firm can be a member of a Section 8 company
Yes, provided the partnership is registered under the Partnership Act
Only if approved by the Central Government
plain.explanation: A partnership firm, being capable of holding property and being a legal person in certain contexts (or association of persons), can be a member of a Section 8 company. Unlike ordinary companies where partnership is sometimes barred, Section 8 allows registered partnerships, associations, and bodies corporate to be members.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following is an accurate statement concerning 'Key Managerial Personnel' (KMP) under Section 2(51)?
options: Every manager of a company is automatically a KMP
Chief Executive Officer is included even if not designated as such
Company Secretary is a KMP
Internal Auditor is statutorily designated as a KMP
plain.explanation: Section 2(51) defines KMP to include: (i) Chief Executive Officer or managing director or manager; (ii) Company Secretary; (iii) Whole-time director; (iv) Chief Financial Officer; and (v) such other officer, not more than one level below the directors who is in whole-time employment, as designated by the Board. Internal auditors are not statutory KMPs.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 2(72), a 'Public Financial Institution' (PFI) includes which of the following institutions?
options: Any cooperative bank operating in rural districts
IDBI Bank Limited
Any foreign investment bank with branches in Mumbai
Any non-banking financial institution registered with SEBI
plain.explanation: Section 2(72) lists specific institutions as Public Financial Institutions, which includes IDBI Bank Limited, LIC, UTI, and specified institutions established under Central Acts.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited is a public company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, with a registered office in Pune. It holds 55% of the total voting power in BioPower Energy Private Limited. BioPower Energy Private Limited, in turn, holds 30% of the total voting power in EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited. GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited also holds a direct 25% voting power in EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited. Furthermore, GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited has an independent nominee agreement giving it significant influence over another firm, AgroInputs India Limited.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the status of BioPower Energy Private Limited in relation to GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited?
options: Associate company
Subsidiary company
Joint venture
Holding company
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 2(87), since GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited controls more than one-half (55%) of the total voting power of BioPower Energy Private Limited, BioPower Energy Private Limited is a subsidiary of GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the relationship between GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited and EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited?
options: EcoSoil is a direct subsidiary of GreenTech
EcoSoil is a subsidiary of GreenTech due to combined voting power control
EcoSoil is completely independent
EcoSoil is a holding company of GreenTech
linkedMcqs.explanation: GreenTech holds 25% directly, and its subsidiary BioPower holds 30%. Under Section 2(87), control of voting power can be exercised on its own or together with one or more of its subsidiary companies (25% + 30% = 55%). Therefore, EcoSoil is a subsidiary of GreenTech.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the status of AgroInputs India Limited in relation to GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited?
options: Subsidiary company
Associate company
Wholly owned subsidiary
Government company
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 2(6), an associate company includes a company in which another company has significant influence, including business control under an agreement. Since GreenTech has an agreement giving it significant influence over AgroInputs, it qualifies as an associate company.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Will BioPower Energy Private Limited be deemed a public company under the Companies Act, 2013 despite being registered as a private company?
options: Yes, because it is a subsidiary of a public company
No, private companies never lose their private status
Yes, provided its turnover exceeds Rs. 200 crores
No, unless its articles are forcibly altered by NCLT
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 2(71), a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company is deemed to be a public company for the purposes of the Act, despite retaining its private corporate form in its articles.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Mr. Raghav, an Indian citizen residing permanently in London for the past 5 years, intends to incorporate a One Person Company (OPC) in Mumbai under the Companies Act, 2013, to engage in software exports. He names his sister, Ms. Ritu (a resident of Delhi and an Indian citizen), as his nominee with her prior written consent. Mr. Raghav proposes to operate the company single-handedly and expects initial paid-up capital of Rs. 40,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Mr. Raghav eligible to incorporate an OPC in India despite residing in London?
options: No, because he has not resided in India for 182 days in the previous year
Yes, since an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise, can incorporate an OPC
No, non-resident Indian citizens are barred from forming an OPC
Yes, provided he obtains prior clearance from the Reserve Bank of India
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the amended rules for One Person Companies, a natural person who is an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise, is eligible to incorporate an OPC.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Ms. Ritu eligible to be appointed as the nominee for Mr. Raghav's OPC?
options: No, because she is a resident of Delhi and Mr. Raghav resides in London
Yes, as she is an Indian citizen and a resident in India, given her written consent
No, siblings cannot be nominees for an OPC
Yes, provided she contributes 50% of the initial capital
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules stipulates that only a natural person who is an Indian citizen and resident in India shall be a nominee for the sole member of a OPC, upon giving prior written consent.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the minimum paid-up share capital requirement for Mr. Raghav's OPC upon incorporation?
options: Rs. 40,000 as proposed, since there is no minimum capital requirement under the Act
linkedMcqs.explanation: With the removal of minimum paid-up capital limits for private and public companies under the Companies Act, 2013, an OPC can be incorporated with any nominal capital, including Rs. 40,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Mr. Raghav simultaneously be a member or nominee in another OPC incorporated by his friend in Bangalore?
options: Yes, up to a maximum of two OPCs
No, a natural person cannot be a member of more than one OPC at any point in time and cannot be a nominee in more than one OPC
Yes, if the business objects of both OPCs are entirely different
No, unless authorized by the Registrar of Companies
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 3 explicitly prohibits a natural person from being a member of more than one OPC at any given time and from being a nominee in more than one OPC.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: HealAndCare Foundation is a company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 to promote advanced medical research and provide free medication to underprivileged cancer patients. The company earns surplus revenues through nominal fees charged for diagnostic camps. Over two financial years, the company accumulated a substantial surplus. The Board of Directors passed a resolution to distribute a 5% dividend to its members and to issue bonus shares to the founding members out of this surplus.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is the Board's decision to distribute a 5% dividend to its members valid under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Valid, since the surplus was earned from diagnostic operations
Valid, provided ordinary resolution is passed in General Meeting
Invalid, because Section 8 companies are prohibited from paying dividends to their members
Valid, up to a maximum ceiling of 10% dividend
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 8 companies are formed with charitable objects and must apply their profits or other income solely in promoting their objects. They are strictly prohibited from paying any dividend to their members.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can HealAndCare Foundation alter its memorandum with respect to its objects without Central Government approval?
options: Yes, by passing a special resolution in a general meeting
No, any alteration of the memorandum or articles of a Section 8 company requires previous approval of the Central Government (or Regional Director)
Yes, provided the ROC is notified within 30 days
No alteration is permitted under any circumstances
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 8(4)(i), a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government (power delegated to Regional Director).

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can HealAndCare Foundation amalgamate with another company that is not a Section 8 company?
options: Yes, freely through a scheme of merger
No, amalgamation is permitted only with another Section 8 company having similar objects
Yes, with NCLT approval
No amalgamation is allowed whatsoever
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the rules, a Section 8 company may only amalgamate with another company registered under Section 8 and having similar objects, ensuring the charitable purpose is not compromised.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If HealAndCare Foundation violates any of the conditions specified in Section 8, what action can the Central Government take?
options: Levy a minor fine on the directors and let the company function
Revoke the license of the company and direct it to wind up or amalgamate with another Section 8 company
Convert the company into a public company automatically without winding up
Imprison the founder members for 7 years
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 8(6), if the company defaults in complying with requirements or violates conditions, the Central Government may revoke its license, after which the company may be wound up or amalgamated with another Section 8 company.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Zenith Real Estate Developers Limited was incorporated in 2018. Due to a prolonged market downturn and pending litigations over title deeds of its major land parcels, the company did not carry on any business or operation, nor did it make any significant accounting transaction during the financial years 2023-24 and 2024-25. The management wishes to keep the corporate entity alive without incurring heavy compliance costs and filing regular operational returns, and thus considers applying for dormant status under Section 455.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Zenith Real Estate Developers Limited eligible to apply for dormant company status under Section 455?
options: No, because it is a public company
Yes, since it has not carried on any business or operation and made no significant accounting transactions for the last two consecutive financial years
No, because it has pending litigations
Yes, provided it obtains a no-objection certificate from all its debtors
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 455 allows a company that has not carried on business or operations or made any significant accounting transactions during the last two consecutive financial years to apply to the Registrar for obtaining dormant status.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What procedural requirement must Zenith fulfill before making an application to the Registrar for dormant status?
options: Pass an ordinary resolution at a general meeting or issue a notice to all shareholders requiring consent
Pass a special resolution in a general meeting or obtain consent of at least 75% shareholders in value
Obtain unanimous consent of all directors only
Appoint a judicial manager through the NCLT
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014 specifies that a company can apply for dormant status only after passing a special resolution at a general meeting or issuing a notice to all shareholders and getting consent of at least 75% in value.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: During the dormant period, which of the following expenses incurred by Zenith will *not* violate its dormant status?
options: Payment of fees to the Registrar of Companies and office maintenance charges
Purchase of new land parcels for future projects
Disbursement of commercial loans to sister concerns
Issuance of new equity shares for cash consideration to expand operations
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 455, payment of statutory fees to the Registrar and payments for maintenance of its office and records do not constitute 'significant accounting transactions' and are permitted for dormant companies.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the maximum continuous period for which a company can remain under a dormant status as per the rules?
options: Three consecutive financial years
Five consecutive financial years
Ten consecutive financial years
Indefinitely until revived by the Registrar
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Rule 7 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014, the maximum period for which a company can remain as a dormant company is restricted to 5 consecutive financial years.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Apex Infrastructure Projects Limited has a complex corporate structure. During a statutory audit, an investigation was initiated regarding non-compliance with corporate filings. The Board of Directors consisted of a Managing Director, three Whole-Time Directors, two Independent Directors, and a Company Secretary. The Chief Financial Officer also participated in board meetings. Due to a failure to file annual financial statements, a penalty notice was issued by the Registrar under the Companies Act, 2013.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Who among the following would be classified as an 'Officer who is in default' under Section 2(60) for the default in filing annual returns?
options: The independent directors in all circumstances
The Managing Director, Whole-Time Directors, Company Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer
Only the external statutory auditor
The external legal consultant who drafted the notices
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(60) designates key managerial personnel such as Managing Directors, Whole-Time Directors, Company Secretaries, and Chief Financial Officers as officers who are in default when contraventions occur.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Will the Independent Directors be held liable as 'officers in default' for the above default?
options: Yes, all directors are jointly and severally liable without exception
No, unless the contravention had occurred with their knowledge, attributable through board processes, or where they had not acted diligently
Yes, because they attended the board meetings
No, independent directors are completely immune to any legal penalties under company law
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(60) explicitly shields independent directors from being designated as officers in default unless the default occurs with their knowledge (attributable through board minutes) or without their exercising adequate due diligence.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What category of personnel does the Company Secretary belong to under Section 2(51)?
options: Key Managerial Personnel
Promoter group
Independent professional
Nominee director
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(51) explicitly lists a Company Secretary as a Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) of the company.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Apex Infrastructure Projects Limited is held to be a company limited by shares. What does this fundamentally imply regarding member liability?
options: Members are liable with their personal residential properties for all corporate debts
Liability of members is limited to the amount unpaid on the shares respectively held by them
Members have zero liability even if shares are partly paid-up
Members must contribute proportionally to corporate losses upon demand by trade creditors
linkedMcqs.explanation: By definition under Section 2(22) or general corporate principles of a company limited by shares, the liability of its members is limited to the amount, if any, unpaid on the shares held by them.
